messages:
alex: quick q — trying to call Redwood from our app inside a customer VPC. they gave us a private endpoint (https://private.redwood-cust.internal) and a custom CA bundle. getting TLS errors in prod only. what is the recommended pattern for SDK config + certs?

maria: two common options depending on stack: set a custom base url + provide the CA to the HTTP client. do NOT use skip_verify in prod. examples: 

python (requests):
```
import os, requests
session = requests.Session()
session.verify = '/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/cust-root.pem'  # or set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
resp = session.post(os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL', 'https://api.redwood.ai') + '/v1/generate', json=payload, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'})
```

node (env):
```
# point SDK at private endpoint
export REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL=https://private.redwood-cust.internal
# for Node.js, include the CA with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or configure https.Agent
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/opt/certs/cust-root.pem
```

go (http.Client):
```
import ("crypto/x509" "io/ioutil" "net/http" "crypto/tls")
caCert, _ := ioutil.ReadFile("/etc/certs/cust-root.pem")
roots := x509.NewCertPool()
roots.AppendCertsFromPEM(caCert)
tr := &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{RootCAs: roots}}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL")+"/v1/chat", bytes.NewBuffer(b))
req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer ...")
client.Do(req)
```

maria: also note: prefer REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL override rather than modifying SDK internals. the SDKs honor the env var or base_url option in client config.

sam: if the customer's network forces traffic through a corporate proxy or an HTTP gateway, you need to set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY for the process or configure the SDK's transport proxy. test connectivity first: 
```
# curl via proxy
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.local:3128 https://private.redwood-cust.internal/v1/health

# raw TLS handshake to verify cert chain
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood-cust.internal:443 -CAfile /etc/certs/cust-root.pem
```

sam: if they use SOCKS, you can use proxychains or a socks5-aware transport. some teams accidentally set only HTTP_PROXY and forget NO_PROXY for metadata endpoints — double-check envs.

jia: streaming quirks we've seen with private endpoints:
- streaming (chunked) requires persistent connections; set keepalive and increase read timeouts on the LB/frontend.
- Node SDK: set streaming: true and ensure your http.Agent has keepAlive: true and maxSockets tuned.

example (node fetch streaming):
```
const controller = new AbortController();
const r = await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL + '/v1/stream', { signal: controller.signal, headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' } });
for await (const chunk of r.body) {
  // handle chunk
}
```

jia: also watch for connection resets if the customer's firewall inspects TLS; sometimes they rewrap certs and you must add their MITM CA to the bundle.

maria: small checklist:
- set REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL to the private endpoint (or pass base_url in client constructor)
- install cust CA into app container and point client to it (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / Go RootCAs)
- configure HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY correctly if proxies exist
- run openssl s_client to validate chain and cipher suites
- do an end-to-end curl test for streaming endpoints (keepalive + chunking)

devx-bot: Docs: <https://internal.redwood.dev/devex/private-endpoints> (internal) — has example env vars and platform notes :book: 

alex: awesome, thanks. one edge-case — our CI runners are in GH actions (outsider IPs) and we need to call the private endpoint only from customer infra. any easy pattern?

maria: use a deploy job that runs inside customer's bastion or trigger a job via their internal runner. alternatively, create a short-lived NAT entry and tightly scope source IPs; avoid embedding certs in public CI.

sam: if you need to debug from CI, use a small container that curls the endpoint through an SSH tunnel: ssh -L 8443:private.redwood-cust.internal:443 bastion@host and curl https://localhost:8443 --cacert /path/to/cust.pem

alex: will try the openssl test and the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS approach first. thanks all :raised_hands:
